main_text.l: Da exempla, in quibus Infinitum po-

l.i: Infinitum potentia secundo modo deprehendi-
tur in tempore & in generatione, item in magni-
tudinibus, secundum appositionem & diuisionem.
His enim semper aliquid addi queat, ut actu nun-

main_text.l: Habetne Infinitum in his se eo-

l.i: Minime. In quibusdam enim conuenit infiniti
ratio, in quibusdam uero plurimum distinguitur.
Quare operæprecium est collationem instituamus.
Primo conuenit infiniti ratio in omnibus, quòd in
ijs semper aliud atque aliud accedit, idq; perpetua
quadam successione. Quod in tempore, in genera-
tione hominum, atque etiam magnitudinibus licet
deprehendere. Differentia autem hæc est: Infinitum
in magnitudinibus per appositionē uel diuisionem
permanet cum prius accepto. Infinitum in tempore
& generatione non permanet cum prius accepto,
sed corrumpitur: quandoquidem aliis definientibus,
siue temporibus, siue hominibus, alia tempora aliisq;
homines sibi succedunt inuicem perpetua serie. Se-
cundo conueniunt aliquo modo infinitum apposi-
tione & infinitum diuisione, rursusq; ab inuicem
differunt. Conueniunt, quòd idem propemodum in-
ter se sunt, quando ex diuisione magnitudinis ac-
crescit

page.notes: Printed text is set in italic throughout the body. The word "ac-" / "accrescit" is broken across lines; I wrote it whole as "accrescit" since the hyphen is at the line end. The reading "aliis" (for "alijs") and "aliisq;" (for "alijq;") are my best reading of the italic forms and are slightly uncertain. The text "Quod in tempore, in generatione" is written with a space added after the comma, as the scan is tight there. Abbreviations q; and & are kept as printed. The line "Infinitum in magnitudinibus" is spaced as in print.
